description.narrative: The Competitiveness Enhancement Project will assist Moldova in enhancing competitiveness of enterprises through improvements in the business environment and making adequate standards, testing and quality improvement services available to enterprises. The project consists of the following components: (i) This component will contribute to the overall government effort in the area of improving business environment and provide strategic input, including continuous support for developing regulatory reform strategy, building institutional capacity for deregulation, and introducing Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) in the legislative process of Moldova. (ii) Addresses product quality obstacles faced by enterprises competing in domestic and international markets related to poor metrology, standardization, testing and quality (MSTQ) infrastructure and services. (iii) This component will help promoting the use of MSTQ services by enterprises, especially small and medium enterprises (SMEs), through the use of the Matching Grants Facility (MGF). (iv) This component will contribute to improving access to finance of private enterprises (mostly SMEs). The project will finance costs of project management, monitoring, financial management, audits and other activities related to overall project management, monitoring and coordination.

The Project will assist Moldova in enhancing competitiveness of enterprises through improvements in the business environment, enhancing access to finance, and making adequate standards, testing, and quality improvement services available to enterprises.

The Law onTechnical Regulations was approved. It foresees the activity and agenda of the technical committees. comment.narrative: As part of the WTO commitments regarding MSTQ system, the Government approved short to medium term (2007-2020) MSTQ Strategy withdetailed action plans for each field of quality infrastructure (Governmental Decision nr. 859 dated 31.07.2006). The Law onTechnical Regulations, which foresees the activity and agenda of the technical committees, was approved. The new Law onStandardization, new Law on Metrology, and the new Law on Accreditation were approved. The institutional reorganization of NISMinto the National Institute of Metrology and National Institute of Standardization is underway. NIM and NIS have been established,and the government is in the process of distributing NISM's assets to NIM and NIS. The government will also establish a SOE thatprovides metrology services across the spectrum, to build the market of service providers and ensure there is some competition inall areas of metrology. (There are 9 private service providers, but some segments of metrology are served by only 1 company). NISM's metrology sector (now NIM) has received the ISO certification in this field (17025), and already has 5 measurementsrecognized in the international CMAC tables, and is working on more. NISM (NIM) was able to achieve this recognition relativelyquickly. There is draft legislation to transpose 6 EU directives, awaiting first discussion in government.
